summary.headline: Manorama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 41.9% YoY to Rs 459 crore and PAT rose 51.8% to Rs 81 crore, with inventory building to Rs 1,000 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 459 crore (up 41.9% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 118 crore (up 34.4%, margin 25.8%) and PAT of Rs 81 crore (up 51.8%, margin 17.6%). H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 863 crore (up 40.8%), EBITDA Rs 224 crore (up 38%) and PAT Rs 159 crore (up 59.2%). Management attributed roughly 85% of growth to volume and 10-15% to price/mix. Inventory rose to Rs 1,000 crore at 30 September 2026 from Rs 728 crore in March, mainly from early procurement of shea and seasonal stock; management expects normalisation in H2. Leadership was restructured, with Deep Saraf moving to MD focused on operations and capacity, and Ashish Saraf moving to business development and strategy.

segments.name: Specialty fats (CBE and Shea stearin)
segments.commentary: Management said CBE and Shea stearin contribute about 70-75% of revenue, up from about 65-70% earlier, with a comfortable range of 70-80% at current capacity. Volume comes mostly from fractionation.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Value-added share of product mix is about 75%, up from 30-35% earlier, with a 70-80% target. Management cited the upgraded fractionation facility and mix as drivers of Q2 growth.

guidance_outlook: Management expects healthy top-line growth for full FY27 and good growth in the coming quarter, but declined to quantify it or to give numeric revenue or EBITDA guidance.
Operating margin band of about 25-27% was described as reasonable, with modest quarter-to-quarter movements possible.
Debottlenecking of existing capacity is expected to be completed by end of FY27, targeting about 85% utilisation on the existing capacity (about 47,500 tonnes).
New capacity (Burkina Faso backward integration, fractionation and LATAM-related expansion) targeted for commissioning around Q3-Q4 FY28, with gradual contribution from FY29.
New capacity to start at 40-50% utilisation and reach 85-90% over 2-3 years.
Asset turnover guided at about 5-7x of investment at optimal utilisation.
Inventory expected to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and to be funded from the existing banking limit and internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Current capex to date is about Rs 70-75 crore, with larger spend expected in H2 FY27 and FY28; no capex was incurred in Q2.
Existing capacity is about 47,500 tonnes at roughly 85% utilisation; a further 45,000 tonnes per annum of debottlenecking is planned.
Burkina Faso backward integration: land acquired, project in design and engineering in-house; detailed update promised in coming quarters.
Fractionation separation plan is in planning and engineering stage; no timeline given.
Management said the greenfield plan and debottlenecking are on track for FY28 Q3-Q4 commissioning, but the timeline was not changed.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no demand slowdown; products are supply-constrained and capacity is fully booked.
About 10-15% of Q2 revenue growth came from price/mix; about 85% from volume. Management said raw-material prices for shea do not track cocoa prices directly.
Freight and logistics costs rose sharply due to shipping and fuel price pressures, which hit gross margin in Q2.
Growth is a mix of new customers and existing customers; new customers are being added in new geographies.
Receivables rose from March 2026 levels, with management attributing this to the last 15 days of September revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of materials rise about 480 bps as a share of revenue while other expenses fell about 360 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is in gross profit, from higher freight costs linked to global macro events and fuel prices. No reclassification was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Q2 revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: About 85% from volume and 10-15% from price realisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there early procurement of shea nuts, and will it recur in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement from newly expanded West African sourcing was in the normal course of business. Management would not commit to limiting it to H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Burkina Faso backward integration and LATAM facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Burkina Faso design is in progress with land acquired. LATAM volumes are gradually ramping from existing capacity, which is fully booked; the LATAM facility timeline is FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex has been spent and when will it be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 70-75 crore has been invested. Commissioning is targeted for Q3-Q4 FY28, with contribution from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue will CBE and shea stearin contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about 70-75%, with a comfortable range of 70-80% at current capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation of new fractionation capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity starts at 40-50% utilisation and reaches 85-90% in 2-3 years. Existing capacity is about 85%.

risks_watch: Inventory of Rs 1,000 crore and rising receivables; watch whether inventory normalises in Q3-Q4 FY27 as management stated.
Freight and fuel cost pressure on gross margin, with no quantified impact given.
Execution risk on the Burkina Faso backward integration and the FY28 Q3-Q4 commissioning timeline; management gave no numeric guidance and project detail is limited.
Leadership transition, with the new MD in his first call and the chairman role changed.
Management declined to give quantified revenue or EBITDA guidance, or the split between new and existing customer growth.
Pricing and realisation trend in renewed contracts; management said there is no direct link to cocoa prices but gave no numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and H1 performance, but evasive on quantification. Management repeatedly declined to give numeric guidance, growth percentages, freight cost impact and capacity detail, and deferred to earlier disclosures or offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Our quarterly revenue is now about Rs. 400 crores.
We are not even giving numeric guidance but we have stated that we believe that we should be clocking 85% kind of utilization for our existing capacities.
So currently that we know because the product what we have minus activities currently are shorting supply only.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management called a 25-27% EBITDA margin band reasonable vs Q2 at 25.8% and H1 at 26%, but freight and fuel costs hit gross margin with no quantified impact, so expansion is not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Debottlenecking adds about 45,000 tpa to existing ~47,500 t, targeted for end FY27; greenfield Burkina Faso/fractionation/LATAM capacity is targeted for Q3-Q4 FY28, though management did not change that timeline and gave no numeric detail.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: About 85% of Q2 revenue growth (41.9% YoY) came from volume, products are supply-constrained, capacity is fully booked and existing utilisation is about 85%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85% and Rs 70-75 crore spent so far, with larger spend guided for H2 FY27 and FY28, and Burkina Faso detail promised in coming quarters.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects healthy FY27 growth and good growth next quarter but gave no numeric guidance, so any upgrade would be qualitative.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rs 1,000 crore inventory (up from Rs 728 crore) and rising receivables depend on normalising in Q3-Q4 FY27, and freight/fuel cost pressure is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or molecule launches were discussed; the call focused on existing CBE, shea stearin and value-added mix.

rows.label: Freight and fuel cost pressure on gross margin
rows.why: Freight and logistics costs rose sharply on shipping and fuel prices and hit Q2 gross margin, with no quantified impact given.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation from Rs 1,000 crore
rows.why: Inventory rose to Rs 1,000 crore from Rs 728 crore in March, and management guided normalisation in Q3-Q4 FY27 funded by banking limits and accruals; gearing is 0.0x with Rs 498 crore cash.

rows.label: New customers and geographies (LATAM ramp)
rows.why: New customers are being added in new geographies and LATAM volumes are ramping from fully booked existing capacity; H1 export mix is 61%.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, supply-constrained order books and H1 performance but evasive on numeric guidance, freight impact and capacity detail; analysts pushed on the cost line mix and the shea early-procurement and inventory build.
